# Shift boot replacement (manual)

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Remove shift knob, pull decorative boot, stretch new boot over shaft, and secure bottom near transmission hole. [t1356]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the shift knob from the top of the shifter.
2. [Partial] Lift and pull away the decorative boot to expose the inner rubber boot connected directly to the transmission opening.
3. Stretch the new boot over the wide upper shaft, using lubricant on the shaft if necessary for a snug fit.
4. Secure the bottom of the boot near the transmission hole; use special clamps or zip ties as needed.

_Procedure reported by [t1356]._

## Tools

- Lubricant [t1356]

## Parts

- Upper Transmission Shift Boot (32862-3S500): Rubber boot connecting directly to the top of the transmission. [t1356]

## Tips & gotchas

- Use tire protectant or similar lubricant on the shifter shaft if the new boot is tight. [t1356]
- Take time when stretching a new boot over the wide upper shaft opening. [t1356]
